keyFindings.description: BlockPointers (:43-54) adds every non-inline node's id to held, including list_item, table rows and cells and a list item's unwritten first paragraph, none of which the renderer gives an offset. For a list item with id X followed by a claim with id X, the claim is uniqueBlocks' node for X. Yet the version write drops its pointers ('mentions X'), while the reconciliation, whose read-back mints a fresh list-item id, writes 'serves X'. CheckBlockPointers skips the pointer the reconciliation stores. Round 4's code wrote 'serves X' on both paths, so this is a regression. Fix: add only typed-block ids to held. Typed blocks always have offsets, and their ids survive the read-back. pointerPairs' BlockType check covers earlier holders that have offsets. Correct the comments at pointers.go:34-37 and :82-84, refs/blocks.go:232-233 and packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:2044-2049.

The BlockPointers skip has no covering test: remove it and every test passes. It is the only guard against a later claim repeating an earlier claim's id, which writes the later claim's pointers as edges from the first claim (round 4's wrong edge, same-type form). Add, on both the version write and the reconciliation: (a) two claims sharing an id, where only the first claim's pointers are edges; (b) a list item then a claim sharing an id, where the claim's pointer is an edge from it and the rows are identical on both paths.

CheckBlockPointers never judges an introduced pointer on a later holder of a typed id. Settlement's EnsureBlockIDs then re-mints that block's id, and the pointer becomes the block's own without having been judged; readers still hide a disallowed target through block_ref_listed. Reaching it needs a repeat the live document already carries. State this consequence where the AGENTS.md paragraph describes the skip.
